source_dataset: seongun/liver-tumor-classification (Hugging Face), derived from the LiTS benchmark (doi:10.1016/j.media.2022.102680), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
dataset_card_statements: label: binary (Normal / Tumor present) assigned based on the segmentation mask
w_sample: windowed CT slice used as network input
why_this_source: liver_final/backend/scripts/build_real_liver_dataset.py downloaded images/w_sample/{i}.png for i = 100..1899 from this dataset and saved them as ct_lits_####.png (numbering continued after the ct_slice files), choosing the folder by brightness rules.

method.environment: The build container could not reach huggingface.co; the verification ran in the user's desktop browser session (same logic as scripts/verify_labels.py --online). Results were transferred to the container as text and checked by SHA-256 on both sides.
method.pixel_matching: For every upstream index 100..1899 the w_sample PNG was decoded (no colour management) and SHA-256 of the 512x512 grey values computed; the 1,745 local ct_lits files (decoded red channel; RGB channels identical) were hashed the same way and aligned in order.
method.label_derivation: Each upstream mask was decoded; label = 1 if any pixel has value 255 (tumour). Compared with metadata.jsonl label.
method.mask_transfer: The 476 tumour-slice masks were reduced to 64x64 three-class maps (argmax of background / liver / tumour pixel counts per 8x8 cell), packed 2 bits per cell, delta-coded between consecutive slices, raw-deflated and base64 encoded (mask_chunk0.txt, mask_chunk1.txt).

results.upstream_indices_without_local_file: 322, 324-326, 328-330, 333-350, 668-697 (55; downloads that failed in the original script)

consequence_for_v8: No-tumour slices contain no liver at all, so slice-level tumour vs no-tumour labels are confounded with liver presence. V8 trains and compares all models on tumour vs tumour-free liver tissue patches defined by the expert masks.
